# Statements on the Consumer Protection Act and the Competition Act · template DC-FS-TM-CPC-006

The two statements a lender files with its licence or registration
application: how it complies with Part VII of the Consumer Protection
Act (credit agreements) and Part VI of the Competition Act (consumer
welfare) (the [licence pack](cbk-licence-pack.md); FS-1095). Each says
what the Part requires and where the lender's policies and the platform
meet it. Read on Kenya Law, 5 November 2026; the two Acts are not yet in
our law register (FS-1097). Built with `tools/policies/build.js`.

## 1. Part VII of the Consumer Protection Act: credit agreements

{{institution_legal}} complies with Part VII of the Consumer Protection Act as follows.

| What Part VII requires | How {{institution}} complies |
|---|---|
| An initial disclosure statement delivered at or before the time the borrower enters the agreement, with the prescribed information | Before signing, every borrower receives the key information document for the product and the agreement with its repayment schedule, the total cost of credit and the annual percentage rate, on their own page; they read and accept the key facts before they can sign (credit, code of ethics and market conduct policy, A.5) |
| No cost of borrowing beyond what the statements disclosed | Every charge is in the product's approved pricing and itemised in the key information document; the platform charges nothing a product version does not contain |
| Representations about credit only as prescribed | Product information is fair, clear and current, and every advertisement and message comes from approved templates |
| A borrower free to buy required insurance from any lawful insurer, and told so in writing | {{insurance}}; the borrower is told in writing that they may buy it from any licensed insurer, and Roan Capital records only that the cover exists and notes its interest |
| A deferral offered only with a statement of whether interest accrues, and at what rate | Any deferral, moratorium or restructuring is agreed in writing with its cost disclosed before it starts (credit policy, A.7, A.8) |
| Default charges limited to reasonable collection and recovery costs | No charge beyond those in the agreement; recovery expenses only those necessary, each itemised; and what is recovered on a non-performing loan never exceeds the cap the lender regulations set |
| The borrower may repay the full balance at any time without charge or penalty, with the unearned cost of borrowing refunded or credited | Early settlement at any time, without penalty, and without interest for the time left to run; the platform computes the settlement amount to the day |
| Errors in statements corrected | Statements come from the ledger; a borrower may ask for one free of charge, and any error is corrected and the correction recorded |

## 2. Part VI of the Competition Act: consumer welfare

{{institution_legal}} complies with Part VI of the Competition Act as follows.

| What Part VI requires | How {{institution}} complies |
|---|---|
| No false or misleading representations in supplying or promoting goods or services | Product information and advertising are approved before use, state the full cost of credit, and never promise approval, speed or terms the product does not give |
| No unconscionable conduct in dealing with consumers or in business transactions | The code of ethics forbids unfair, deceptive, oppressive or aggressive practices; collection never harasses, shames or threatens; no product is tied to another; refusals are given at once, with reasons |
| Consumer complaints handled, and referable to the Competition Authority | A complaints mechanism made known to every customer, each complaint acknowledged and resolved within the times the regulations set, the customer told they may escalate to the Central Bank of Kenya; Roan Capital cooperates with any inquiry by the Competition Authority |

## 3. Declaration

{{institution_legal}} confirms that its policies and its lending platform are designed to meet these requirements, that its staff are trained in them, and that compliance is reviewed at least once a year by its board.
